posts.name: DavePel
posts.cooked:
My playgroup and I are new to the game, and we have a question about beating Baron Blade.

When we take his first side out, and flip him. If he has 4HP and we do 12 DMG, does his flipped side start with 30, or do we continue that DMG and keep rolling with 22HP?
posts.raw:
My playgroup and I are new to the game, and we have a question about beating Baron Blade.

When we take his first side out, and flip him. If he has 4HP and we do 12 DMG, does his flipped side start with 30, or do we continue that DMG and keep rolling with 22HP?

posts.name: Pydro
posts.cooked: He goes to 30. Blade was at 4 and you deal Blade 12 damage. This brings Blade to -8. Now, since his hp is lower than 0, he is destroyed, but his card says to flip him instead, and restore him to 30. All damage is dealt at once, so Blade takes the entire 12, then you see about other triggers.
posts.raw: He goes to 30. Blade was at 4 and you deal Blade 12 damage. This brings Blade to -8. Now, since his hp is lower than 0, he is destroyed, but his card says to flip him instead, and restore him to 30. All damage is dealt at once, so Blade takes the entire 12, then you see about other triggers.

posts.name: Reckless
posts.cooked:
Also, if Blade is dealt 1 & 1 damage (Fanatic’s innate, for instance) at 1 HP he would flip but not be dealt the second instance of damage because he is technically a “new” target.

That’s right, isn’t it?
posts.raw:
Also, if Blade is dealt 1 & 1 damage (Fanatic's innate, for instance) at 1 HP he would flip but not be dealt the second instance of damage because he is technically a "new" target.

That's right, isn't it?

posts.cooked: If it is a different target, things like Twist the Ether would be destroyed when he flips. However, I do think it is the same target. The card says to "restore baron Blade to 30 hp." At least to me, it seems like it is the same "Baron Blade," and you are restoring his hp.

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked: Blade is still the same target, he is not a new target entering play. If flipping a card is a new target entering play, then Omnitron triggers Hairtrigger Reflexes so many times!

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
Christopher ruled this for me during the introduction to GSF boogle chat: I asked about the talisman flipping and the interaction thereof with bounties, and he told me that a flipping target is still the same target, so it is not leaving or entering play, but merely changing gameplay text.

Following this logic, Exorcism would continue on Blade’s flip side.

Following this logic, Exorcism would continue on Blade's flip side.

posts.cooked: Yeah, we've always played it that blade takes that second hit. So if that 12 points mentioned in the original post was actually two instances of damage (6 and 6), he'd take the first 6, go to 0 (or -2), flip, resest to 30, and take the second 6.
